theory.intro: A volume conversion uses the length factor **cubed**. A metre is $100$ cm, so a cubic metre is $100$ cm by $100$ cm by $100$ cm, or $1\,000\,000$ cubic centimetres. Every capacity step is a factor of $1000$.
facts: The volume ladder runs $\text{m}^3$, $\text{cm}^3$, $\text{mm}^3$ from largest unit to smallest.
The capacity ladder runs ML, kL, L, mL from largest unit to smallest, and each step is $\times 1000$ or $\div 1000$.
Volume and capacity are linked by $1\text{ cm}^3 = 1$ mL, $1000\text{ cm}^3 = 1$ L and $1\text{ m}^3 = 1$ kL.
Moving to a **smaller** unit **multiplies**; moving to a **larger** unit **divides**.
The factor is never the length factor and never the area factor: $\text{cm}^3 \to \text{m}^3$ divides by $100^3$, not $100$ or $100^2$.
steps: Find the two units on the volume ladder or the capacity ladder. If converting between volume and capacity, use $1\text{ cm}^3 = 1\text{ mL}$ or $1\text{ m}^3 = 1\text{ kL}$ to move between the ladders.
Decide to multiply (to a smaller unit) or divide (to a larger unit) for any remaining ladder steps.
Apply the factor: the length factor cubed for a volume step, $1000$ for a capacity step.

workedExamples.question_text: A cube has edges of length $1$ cm, or $10$ mm. Explain why $1\text{ cm}^3=1000\text{ mm}^3$. Then explain why $1\text{ m}^3=1\,000\,000\text{ cm}^3$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Count the unit cubes along each of the three dimensions.
$\begin{aligned}V&=10\times10\times10\\&=1000\text{ mm}^3\end{aligned}$
A metre is $100$ cm, so a cube with edges of length $1$ m has volume
$\begin{aligned}V&=100\times100\times100\\&=1\,000\,000\text{ cm}^3.\end{aligned}$
The length factor is cubed because volume has three dimensions. Multiply when converting to smaller units; divide when converting to larger units.

workedExamples.question_text: Convert (a) $6.4\text{ cm}^3$ to $\text{mm}^3$ and (b) $720\,000\text{ cm}^3$ to $\text{m}^3$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Cubic millimetres are smaller, so multiply by $10^3$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}6.4\times10^3\\&=6400\text{ mm}^3\end{aligned}$
(b) Cubic metres are larger, so divide by $100^3$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}720\,000\div100^3\\&=0.72\text{ m}^3\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Convert (a) $0.024\text{ m}^3$ to $\text{mm}^3$ and (b) $280\,000\text{ mm}^3$ to $\text{m}^3$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Convert through cubic centimetres, multiplying at each step.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}0.024\times100^3\times10^3\\&=24\,000\times1000\\&=24\,000\,000\text{ mm}^3\end{aligned}$
(b) Convert through cubic centimetres, dividing at each step.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}280\,000\div10^3\div100^3\\&=280\div1\,000\,000\\&=0.00028\text{ m}^3\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Convert (a) $4.8$ kL to L and (b) $625$ mL to L.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Litres are smaller than kilolitres, so multiply by $1000$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4.8\times1000\\&=4800\text{ L}\end{aligned}$
(b) Litres are larger than millilitres, so divide by $1000$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}625\div1000\\&=0.625\text{ L}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Convert (a) $760\,000$ L to ML and (b) $0.36$ kL to mL.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Move from L to kL, then from kL to ML.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}760\,000\div1000\div1000\\&=760\div1000\\&=0.76\text{ ML}\end{aligned}$
(b) Move from kL to L, then from L to mL.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}0.36\times1000\times1000\\&=360\times1000\\&=360\,000\text{ mL}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Convert (a) $485\text{ cm}^3$ to mL, (b) $1.62\text{ m}^3$ to L, (c) $7350\text{ cm}^3$ to kL and (d) $2.8$ L to $\text{cm}^3$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Use $1\text{ cm}^3=1\text{ mL}$.
$485\text{ cm}^3=485\text{ mL}$
(b) Use $1\text{ m}^3=1\text{ kL}$, then convert to litres.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}1.62\text{ m}^3\\&=1.62\text{ kL}\\&=1620\text{ L}\end{aligned}$
(c) Use $1\text{ cm}^3=1\text{ mL}$, then divide by $1000$ for each capacity step.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}7350\text{ cm}^3\\&=7350\text{ mL}\\&=7.35\text{ L}\\&=0.00735\text{ kL}\end{aligned}$
(d) Convert litres to millilitres, then use $1\text{ mL}=1\text{ cm}^3$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2.8\text{ L}\\&=2800\text{ mL}\\&=2800\text{ cm}^3\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A container holds $1600$ mL of water. After $0.65$ L is poured out, how much water remains, in millilitres?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Convert the amount poured out to millilitres.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}0.65\times1000\\&=650\text{ mL}\end{aligned}$
Subtract amounts in the same unit.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}1600-650\\&=950\text{ mL}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A $2.4$ L bottle of juice is poured into cups that each hold $350$ mL. How many full cups can be filled?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Convert the juice to millilitres.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2.4\times1000\\&=2400\text{ mL}\end{aligned}$
Divide by the capacity of one cup.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2400\div350\\&=6.857142\ldots\end{aligned}$
There is enough juice for $6$ full cups.

foundation.question_text: To convert a volume from $\text{cm}^3$ to $\text{mm}^3$, do you multiply or divide, and by what factor?
foundation.solution_text:
A cubic millimetre is smaller than a cubic centimetre, so the count of them is larger and the conversion multiplies.
The length factor is $10$, and a volume needs it cubed.
Multiply by $10^3 = 1000$.

foundation.question_text: To convert a volume from $\text{cm}^3$ to $\text{m}^3$, do you multiply or divide, and by what factor?
foundation.solution_text:
A cubic metre is larger than a cubic centimetre, so the count of them is smaller and the conversion divides.
The length factor is $100$, and a volume needs it cubed.
Divide by $100^3 = 1\,000\,000$.
